questions.label: Q1
questions.question: Is a bicycle among the stolen or damaged items?

questions.label: Q2
questions.question: Does the file state that household contents were stolen or damaged by a theft outside the insured location that was neither a burglary (the thief forcibly entered the building or a room of it, or broke open a container in it, or unlocked it with the correct keys or codes that the thief had obtained by burglary or robbery; a vehicle is not a container) or a robbery (theft under threat or use of violence against the policyholder or a member of the household, or while they could not resist because of unconsciousness, accident or death; pickpocketing and trick theft are not robbery)?

questions.label: Q3
questions.question: Does the file state that measures to reduce the loss are still to be taken (not yet carried out)?

questions.label: Q4
questions.question: Does the file state that the measures could not wait for the insurer's instruction because of imminent danger (Gefahr im Verzug)?

questions.label: Q5
questions.question: Does the file state that the original purchase vouchers for all of the stolen or damaged items cannot be obtained, or only at considerable cost (not even as a duplicate from the seller)?

questions.label: Q6
questions.question: Does the policy, or the file, show that the policy does not include the separate supplementary insurance for simple theft away from home (einfacher Diebstahl auswärts)?

questions.label: Q7
questions.question: Does the file state that traces of the theft (for example pry marks, a broken lock, window or container) have been removed or altered, or are to be removed or altered, by the policyholder or on their behalf, for example by repair or cleaning?

text:
Dear Ms Zimmermann,

I think there's been a mix-up in how my claim was taken down on the phone, so I'd like to set it straight in writing.

This was a break-in at home, in my own flat at Mühleweg 77 in St. Gallen. On Tuesday 11 August 2026 I was at work from eight until half past five. When I got home, the balcony door was standing open. Someone had climbed up onto the first-floor balcony and levered the door open with a tool, and inside they'd gone through every room. They took my laptop, two watches, a camera and some cash from the desk, about CHF 9,450 in total. My neighbour Sophie Reid called the police for me because my hands were shaking too much.

There was nothing I had to do urgently afterwards. Nothing was at risk of getting worse, so I didn't arrange anything on my own and I'm waiting for your instructions on what happens next.

The flat is still the way I found it. I haven't had the balcony door repaired, and I haven't cleaned up the marks on the frame or tidied the rooms the thieves went through. I've been sleeping at a friend's place for now, because I don't feel at ease there at the moment.

Please let me know when someone from CSS can come and look at it.

Kind regards,
Henry Shaw
